slides.text: At two in the afternoon I noticed three Instagram posts hadn't gone up — 6am, 9am, noon, all missed.

citations.quote: At two in the afternoon I noticed three Instagram posts hadn't gone up — 6am, 9am, noon, all missed.

slides.text: The job had been crashing on every single run, without exception, since the day I'd first set it up. Same error every time: macOS quietly refusing it read access to a folder on my Desktop, forty-four times over.

citations.quote: The job had been crashing on every single run, without exception, since the day I'd first set it up.

slides.text: When I ran the exact same script by hand, from my own terminal, it worked. My shell already had the permission — granted once, years ago, without me thinking about it.

citations.quote: when I ran the exact same script by hand, from my own terminal, it worked

slides.text: I'd tested the script. I hadn't tested the absence of me.

citations.quote: I hadn't tested the absence of me.

slides.text: Kieran Klaassen has a name for the order: build it, use it, trust it, and then orchestrate it.

citations.quote: build it, use it, trust it, and then orchestrate it

slides.text: One item on Klaassen's failure list — agents sitting frozen on "working" with no signal anything's wrong — has the same silent-failure shape as one job crashing forty-four times.

citations.quote: agents sitting frozen on "working" with no signal anything's wrong
the failure that survives every manual test is the one you only meet in the room you stopped standing in

slides.text: Jake Van Clief works on that half: breaking a process into stages that hand off to each other, where each stage does exactly one job and nothing moves to the next stage without a person checking the handoff first.

citations.quote: breaking a process into stages that hand off to each other, where each stage does exactly one job and nothing moves to the next stage without a person checking the handoff first

slides.text: And before you walk away, test one more thing: does it still work when you're no longer in the room? Mine didn't.

citations.quote: does it still work when you're no longer in the room
